title: Chicken Shawarma
subtitle: Spiced chicken thighs roasted until caramelised
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs marinated in warm Middle Eastern spices, lemon, and garlic then roasted at high heat until the edges char and caramelise. Served with yoghurt and flatbread, this is one of the most reliably impressive weeknight dinners.
sourceNotes: Shawarma is a Levantine street food descended from the Ottoman doner kebab, adapted across the Middle East, North Africa, and beyond. The word comes from the Turkish cevirme, meaning turning. Home oven versions that replicate the flavour of the rotating spit through high-heat roasting have become a modern classic across the region and diaspora.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate for up to 24 hours in the fridge for deeper flavour.

content.text: Use a hot oven and do not crowd the tray. Space the chicken thighs so the heat can circulate around them. Crowding causes steaming rather than roasting.

items.prepNote: 1 juiced, 1 cut into wedges to serve

content.text: Mix all the marinade ingredients together in a large bowl with a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Add the chicken thighs and turn to coat. Leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 24 hours in the fridge.
Preheat the oven to 220 C. Arrange the chicken thighs on the baking tray in a single layer without overlapping. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes until the edges are deeply coloured and slightly charred.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then slice thinly. Serve with Greek yoghurt, lemon wedges, and flatbread.

items.symptom: Chicken is pale and steamed rather than roasted
items.fix: Use a large tray and space the chicken out so air can circulate.
Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight for best results.
Check at 25 minutes. Remove when juices run clear and edges are charred.
